a: Take regular backups and test restores — untested backups are risky.
PITR restores a database to a specific timestamp using base backup + WAL.
Read replicas serve read traffic and improve scalability, with possible lag.
DB max connections can be exhausted; use pooling (PgBouncer, etc.).
Slow query logs identify expensive SQL for indexing and rewrite.
Prefer expand/contract migrations to avoid long locks and downtime.
Online DDL changes schema with minimal locking when supported.
ANALYZE updates planner stats; VACUUM reclaims dead tuples (Postgres).
Hot standby servers can serve reads while replaying replication.
Failover promotes a replica when the primary fails.
RPO is max acceptable data loss; RTO is max acceptable downtime.
Encrypt data files/disks so stolen media is unreadable without keys.
